current.text: Fred VanVleet is back, so Thompson moves off point guard and plays closer to the rim.
He is in the projected starting five with VanVleet, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Sengun.
With less time at point guard, his assists may drop by about one per game.
Off the ball, his blocks, steals and rebounds should come back. Lloyd hopes for about 0.9 blocks and a field goal percentage of 55 to 56%.

Lloyd says he is a mid-to-late second-round pick in category leagues if his blocks and field goal percentage improve. If not, he is a third-round pick, around 28 to 30. An ESPN rank of 13 is slightly aggressive.
Josh values him close to 40 USD. In an auction mock he went for 35 USD, which Josh did not call an overpay.
He is falling in drafts, possibly because of his preseason.
Ime Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes.
With our March 28 end, the Rockets have a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over three weeks.
Houston is predicted to win 54 games.

durable.text: He is an elite athlete who makes almost no threes and is far from a reliable outside shot.
He is a highly efficient finisher, with a field goal percentage well above other guards.
He is a low scorer for his draft range and is unlikely to score 20 a game.
His blocks drive his value. He adds rim deterrence, but his blocks drop when he plays point guard.
He rebounds and blocks shots far more than other guards.
He is worth clearly more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: The market prices him at 31 to 36 USD (Yahoo average cost 30.9 USD, ESPN 35.7 USD), below the 38 USD our league paid last season and Josh's value of about 40 USD. Since he is sliding in drafts, 35 to 38 USD is a fair price. He fits punt 3PM builds best: he gives strong FG% on 13 shots a game plus rebounds, steals and blocks from a guard slot. In the first weeks, check whether his blocks get back near 0.9 and his FG% reaches 55% now that he is off the ball. Also keep in mind that Houston's 3-3-4 playoff schedule is weak.
